Before P169, memory was not bounded and nothing recorded that stdout was cut.

Before P169, Client.graphql returned OK with no data on a cut body, because classify says OK on exit 0, so PullFiles reported 'not found, or you cannot see it'.
Before P169, SetFilesViewed (out == nil) read a cut body as success.
In ghclient only four gh calls carry a body: PullsForCommit, PullsForBranch, OpenPulls and PullFiles.
PullsForCommit uses REST commits/{sha}/pulls?per_page=10; PullsForBranch uses REST pulls?head=…&per_page=5.
OpenPulls uses REST pulls?state=open&per_page=100&page=1..3.
PullFiles uses GraphQL files(first:100) projecting only path and viewerViewedState, under 1 MiB per page.

The real size exposure is OpenPulls, with 100 full pull objects per page; no REST call fetches files or reviews.
Estimated OpenPulls pull item without body is about 15-30 KiB (arithmetic, not measured).
A pull body is max 65536 chars, about 384 KiB JSON-escaped worst case; per-item worst case is about 450 KiB (estimate).

P169 rejected per-endpoint --jq projection: D4 (G24 plan) rejected --jq as a second expression language kept in step with rawPull.
P169 also rejected --jq because classify reads GitHub's error body from stdout, so a filter could lose the SSO/scope message.

P169 decision (Option C): raise gh stdout cap to 64 MiB (maxStdoutBytes = 64<<20), enforced while reading.
The 64 MiB cap derives from the about 45 MiB OpenPulls worst-case page; same figure as Studio import cap and Wails streamMaxFrameBytes.
maxStderrBytes stays 1 MiB.
maxStdoutBytes and maxStderrBytes become vars, not consts, so tests can lower them.
With the P169 cap, memory grows only with real output; D4 stays as written, with no new dependency, rate-limit change or wire-type change.
ghclient runner uses an unexported boundedWriter (bytes.Buffer, max, overflow flag) for cmd.Stdout and cmd.Stderr.
boundedWriter.Write appends up to remaining capacity, sets overflow when bytes are dropped, and always returns len(p), nil.
boundedWriter.Write must never return an error: that would stop the os/exec copy goroutine, close the pipe and SIGPIPE gh, giving a failed exit instead of 'too large'.
Result gains StdoutTruncated bool, set on both exit-0 and ExitError returns; zero value keeps fake Runners compiling.
gitclient has a similar writer type, but it is unexported in another package with stderr-marker logic, so it is not shared.
ghclient classify, when res.StdoutTruncated (checked after the runErr branch, before exit-0), returns Status{Kind: KindForbidden, Reason: tooLargeReason()}.
tooLargeReason() is a func, not const, producing "GitHub's response was over %d MiB, too large to read" from maxStdoutBytes>>20.

stored.fact: internal/llmprompts holds every LLM prompt and LLM-facing instruction that both apps (Space and Studio) send.
internal/llmprompts is not internal/prompts, which is the P246 popup router.
registry.go is the only file containing prompt text.
A registry entry has: id, kind, apps, title/purpose/usedBy catalog keys, applies-when, default, required fragments, fixed output schema.
Registry entries are accessed through the typed handle Prompt[V] with Text(src, vars).
Registry entries without variables use NoVars.
Registry entry kinds: system, message, suffix, instructions, tool, argument, toolResult, fragment.
Kind argument is one MCP tool property description and carries Parent tool and Field.
Kind fragment is included via {{template}}.
The prompt registry excludes user-authored text: smart-script bodies, workflow stage prompts and step prompts.
The prompt registry also excludes tool and server names, tool error strings, and result data formatting.
InputSchema[T] sets each MCP tool property's description from its argument registry entry.
A mismatch between a tool property and its argument entry panics at server build.
jsonschema tags are not used.
Prompt templates use text/template, one template set per resolve, with only the funcs inc and join.
An entry with NoVars and no fragments is literal and never parsed.
The default prompt renders byte-identical to pre-P271 output (testdata/golden).
RenderParts wraps each string variable in marker runes and splits, so Settings Preview marks resolved values with VarText.
A failed RenderParts self-check returns one literal part.
Prompt overrides are stored per app in <home>/llm-prompts.json (~/.kira-studio/, ~/.kira-space/).
llm-prompts.json is written with renameio, mode 0600.
llm-prompts.json shape: {version, revision, overrides: {id: {text, defaultHash, updatedAt}}}.
Saving the default text removes the prompt override.
Prompt override text must be 1 byte to 32 KiB.
A prompt change carries baseHash, and a stale change is refused with E_CONFLICT.
If the prompt store file is corrupt or an override no longer validates, the default is used and a warning is logged.
Settings flags a corrupt store or invalid override with storeError and invalid.
defaultChanged flags an override made against an older default.
Server-side override validation requires the template parses and executes against example vars.
Server-side override validation requires every prompt:"required" variable referenced and every required fragment included.
Memory system prompts must include fragment memory.dataHygiene, which is the injection defence.
Schema-bound prompts (gate, reconcile, import extract and finalize) keep their JSON schema fixed, shown read-only in Settings.
There is no global prompt source.
Consumers receive a llmprompts.Source (Resolve, Revision) through options.
Consumers of llmprompts.Source: memory.ServiceOptions, mcpserver.Options, claudeheadless, scriptruns, ADE, dbmcp.
Defaults() is the registry-only source.
Store.Resolve stats the file per call and re-reads on mtime or size change.
Gate, reconcile, import, headless suffixes and ADE messages resolve per call, so a prompt edit applies on the next call.
memory-mcp is a stdio subprocess; memorycli.Run gets <KiraSpaceHome>/llm-prompts.json.
memory-mcp builds server instructions, tool and argument descriptions once per process, so edits apply to new Claude sessions.
dbmcp and claudeheadless rebuild their MCP server when Revision() changes.
Prompt IPC is LlmPromptsService (List, Save, Preview) in both apps, plus event kira:llmPrompts:changed {revision}.
Save is all-or-nothing, with per-id errors returned as an E_BAD_REQUEST payload.
Preview with real vars also renders the ADE run dialog and step inspector, so no TS copy of a prompt exists.
Settings section Prompts sits before Advanced in both apps, in packages/workbench/src/llmPrompts/.
The Prompts section has a list, Monaco editor, Changes diff against default, Preview, and per-entry reset.
Drafts live in Pinia store llmPromptDrafts.
Dialog Save saves prompts first, then the settings patch.
Guard go run ./internal/llmprompts/cmd/checkprompts is part of bun run lint.
checkprompts fails on a jsonschema tag.
checkprompts fails on an mcp.Tool, mcp.Prompt or mcp.PromptArgument Description, or mcp.ServerOptions Instructions, not from llmprompts.
checkprompts fails on a memory.Call System not from llmprompts.
checkprompts fails on a copy of a registry default in a non-test .go, .ts or .vue file outside internal/llmprompts and internal/flowtest.
Copy detection matches the first 48 characters of a registry default, or the whole text when it is 24 to 47 characters.

stored.fact: Kira Studio is a native macOS workbench built on Wails (Go) and Vue 3.
Kira Studio is a visual database client for ten engines plus an HTTP/gRPC API client.
Kira Studio modes are Studio (database), Api, Automations and Docker, switched with one button.
The repo also contains sibling app Kira Space: git client and code workspace with coding agents (ADE), memory store, terminal, and phone view on home network.
Kira Space docs are in apps/kira-space/README.md.
Kira Studio supports only macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon (arm64), dark mode only.
Kira Studio builds are ad-hoc signed, not notarized.
Kira Studio does not ship light mode, Windows/Linux, DDL editing, CSV/JSON result export, connection folders, split editor groups, SSH tunneling, code signing or notarization.
Each new Kira Studio build counts as a different app to macOS Keychain, so first launch after an update may prompt for Keychain access.
Choose Always Allow once per build at the Keychain prompt.
Saved credentials are encrypted at rest in Keychain; Touch ID or system password is required to reveal a saved password.
Install with scripts/install.sh using --app=studio, or --app=space for Kira Space.
install.sh downloads the latest release disk image, moves the app to /Applications and opens it without a Gatekeeper prompt, unlike a browser-downloaded DMG.
The app checks GitHub for a newer release and offers an update.
There is deliberately no silent auto-update; nothing installs until the user clicks Update.
Build from source with `bun run package:studio`, which installs its own dependencies first (Bun workspace, Go module, pinned wails3 CLI).
Build output is apps/kira-studio/bin/Kira Studio.app and Kira Studio.dmg.
A locally built app needs a Gatekeeper workaround on first launch: right-click Open, or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine` on the app.
Packaging details are in docs/PACKAGING.md.
PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MySQL (8.0.16+) and SQLite have grid view, SQL console and writes.
ClickHouse has grid view, SQL console and insert-only writes.
MongoDB has documents view, shell-style console and writes.
Redis has key/value view and Redis commands console; writes on string keys, delete on any type.
Kafka has stream view, no console, produce only.
SQS has stream view, no console, send and delete.
S3 has object browser, no console, writes plus upload/download.
Stop cancels the operation itself (pg_cancel_backend, KILL QUERY, cursor abort, consumer stop), not only its display.
SQS never polls on its own; it reads only on Poll press.
SQS reads only on demand because ReceiveMessage hides messages from real consumers.
Connections support fields or URI mode, and test-connection.
Each connection has a read-only guard enforced in the backend.
Connections support an optional pre-connect script, e.g. port-forward.
Connections can be imported from a JetBrains DataGrip project.
Paste credentials accepts labelled text, .env lines or psql/mysql-style command; review, then apply.
Update credentials on a saved connection changes only username and password.
The same table can open in any number of tabs, each with its own paging, sort, filter and scroll.
Session restore reopens tabs without auto-connecting.
Data grid is virtualized in both directions, with page sizes 10 to 10k.
Data grid offers count-all on request, column projection, and in-page find.
Data grid supports server-side WHERE/ORDER BY with history and saved filters.
Cell editor is a Monaco panel detecting JSON, XML, SQL, base64, hex, epoch seconds/milliseconds, ISO-8601 and CSV, with beautify and compact.
Staged SQL edits form a pending change set with exact command preview; nothing reaches the database until commit.
Document, key/value and stream writes apply immediately.
Foreign-key navigation works on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite.
Foreign-key navigation can preview the referenced row in a popover, open it in a pre-filtered tab, or jump to editing.
Query console is per-connection, with run-statement, run-all, saved queries and Format.
Query console offers EXPLAIN for every SQL dialect and optional auto-explain flagging expensive queries.
Console completions, diagnostics and hovers come from a pasted DDL document.
Column masking (PII) has six masks with live preview; it is display-only and data is never changed.
Generate data fills a SQL table with fake rows using per-column recipes inferred from types.
Operations panel shows live operations with duration, rows, command, cancel and re-run, plus a persisted operation log.
Caching has three tiers with no speculative prefetch; see docs/PERF.md.
Kira Studio supports multiple windows (⇧⌘N) and a command palette (⇧⌘P).
Automations scripts are grouped in collections.
Each automation script runs in its own folder under app home (or a chosen folder), with run history (status, exit code, result).
A smart script is a prompt run by headless Claude Code.
Smart scripts have typed parameters (text, select, multi-select, secret), model, budget, timeout, and a tick list of allowed tools and MCP servers.
Scripts can recur on a cron schedule.
A due scheduled run asks confirmation by default, and a missed run is never replayed.
Api client request builder has method, URL, params, headers, and body (raw, JSON/XML/HTML/JS, form-urlencoded, multipart, binary file).

Runner schedules bulk imports through the stages scan, materialise, extract, finalize.
Exactly one Runner runs per memory.db, enforced by an exclusive flock.
Runner follows job rows that the control side (Engine) writes, by polling.
Pause or cancel from another process takes effect within one tick.
All Runner state lives in memory.db.
A halted runner resumes from disk.
NewRunner takes no lock.
Run takes the store's runner lock and works until ctx ends or the store is idle for IdleExit.
A runner taking the lock resets what a crashed predecessor left mid-flight.

The runner never resumes a job by itself.
Runner.tryExit releases the lock, then looks once more for work a control call wrote meanwhile.
